topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular context of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutation acquisition can lead to cancer when affected cells have the capacity and conditions to evolve.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk and its interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how confidently cancer risk can be attributed to environmental exposure rather than chance or inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the general account into a detailed example.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmentally induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through processes that can depend on cellular metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Tissue susceptibility and summary of carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The discussion of host susceptibility completes the mechanistic account of carcinogenesis that the following subtopic summarises.

topics.label: Evidence linking human carcinogen exposure to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human samples and populations can connect carcinogen exposure with cancer development.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate how controlled experimental tests detect carcinogenic potential and why their results may not capture human cancer risk.

topics.label: Concluding summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about carcinogenic risk and places them within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
